coverage: Coverage is thinner before 2016: about 49 Technology members per quarter in 2011Q4–2015Q4, against about 75 from 2021. Part of the gap is real (the sector's weight in the index grew), but FMP has no balance sheets for several Technology companies acquired in 2012–2018, including BMC Software, CA Technologies, EMC, Molex, Tellabs, CSRA and Harman, and LSI and Novellus could not be matched to FMP tickers. These were mostly mature, profitable companies, so their absence may tilt the early-period results.
holdout_comment: The holdout picks are weaker in the test window than the walk-forward results suggest. The single 2021–2025 test period is dominated by one regime, which is why model size and expected performance are judged on walk-forward testing instead.
chosen_rationale: **Three metrics** is the size supported by walk-forward testing (Section 9.4).

**Statistically strongest.** They are the top two 3-metric models on the full sample and the only ones with an adjusted t near 3, i.e. still significant after allowing for the number of models searched.
**Consistent across regimes.** IC is positive in every era, including 2011–2015, when profitability metrics such as ROE and ROIC predicted in reverse.

**Reliable inputs.** All three metrics are cash-flow based (free cash flow payout, cash-flow growth, capex relative to operating cash flow), which depend less on accounting choices and are more comparable across companies than earnings-based measures.
**Smoothed capex.** The 3-year capex intensity averages out one-off spending years; it raised the t of the otherwise identical 1-year version from 4.40 to 5.14.
chosen_notes: **Top vs second choice.** The two are statistically level and share two of three metrics, so they rank companies similarly. The top choice uses operating cash-flow growth, which keeps growth separate from investment; the second uses free-cash-flow growth, which already subtracts capex, so capex enters the second model twice. The second choice has the milder worst year and the clearest gain over its 2-metric parts.

**A diversifying alternative.** FCF_Payout_Ratio | CFOPS_CAGR_3Yr + Asset_G_Rate_5Yr (low 5-year total-asset growth, the Fama-French direction) is the most stable model in 2011–2015 and has the mildest worst year, but a weaker adjusted t. It could serve as a check that behaves differently from the chosen pair.
limitations: **Regime dependence.** Profitability metrics reversed in 2011–2015 and asset growth reversed in 2021–2025. The chosen models were stable across eras, but there is no guarantee the next regime will behave like the past ones.
**Early coverage.** Several acquired Technology companies are missing before 2016 (Section 3.6).
